akhfash:4-6.t: He said ﴿فِيهَا يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ﴾ ﴿أَمْراً﴾, and He said ﴿رَحْمَةً مِّن رَّبِّكَ﴾: their accusative is on the basis of "We sent it down as a command and a mercy", as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

akhfash:42-42.t: And He said ﴿إِلاَّ مَن رَّحِمَ ٱللَّهُ إِنَّهُ هُوَ﴾: he made it a badal (substitute) for the implied pronoun in ﴿يُنصَرُونَ﴾. If you wish, you make it a mubtadaʾ (subject) and imply its khabar (predicate), meaning "except one on whom Allah has mercy, for (that) will avail him".

akhfash:54-54.t: And He said ﴿وَزَوَّجْنَاهُم بِحُورٍ عِينٍ﴾: He means — and Allah knows best — "We made them pairs with the ḥūr". Some Arabs say "عين حير".

daas-irab:1-10.t: ﴿حم وَالْكِتابِ الْمُبِينِ﴾ the i'rab of its like has already been given; ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿أَنْزَلْناهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is resumptive; ﴿فِي لَيْلَةٍ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb; ﴿مُبارَكَةٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿كُنَّا﴾ kāna and its noun; ﴿مُنْذِرِينَ﴾ its khabar, and the verbal clause is the khabar of إنا, and the nominal clause is resumptive; ﴿فِيها﴾ both attached to what follows them; ﴿يُفْرَقُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb; ﴿كُلُّ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ﴿أَمْرٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation); ﴿حَكِيمٍ﴾ an adjective of أمر, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿أَمْراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb; ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِنا﴾ both attached to an omitted adjective of أمرا; ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿كُنَّا مُرْسِلِينَ﴾ kāna, its noun and its khabar, and the verbal clause is the khabar of إنا, and the nominal clause is resumptive; ﴿رَحْمَةً﴾ mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative (manṣūb); ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ both attached to رحمة; ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿هُوَ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); ﴿السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ﴾ two khabars of inna, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl); ﴿رَبِّ﴾ a badal (substitute) for ربك; ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to السموات; ﴿وَما﴾ conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿بَيْنَهُما﴾ an adverb of place attached to an omitted verb forming the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative; ﴿إِنْ﴾ a conditional that makes the verb jussive; ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun; ﴿مُوقِنِينَ﴾ its khabar, and the clause كنتم is initial (ibtidāʾiyya); ﴿لا﴾ negative, operating like inna; ﴿إِلهَ﴾ its noun, and its khabar is omitted; ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿هُوَ﴾ a badal for the noun of لا; ﴿يُحْيِي﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿وَيُمِيتُ﴾ conjoined to يحيي; ﴿رَبُّكُمْ﴾ badal; ﴿وَرَبُّ﴾ conjoined; ﴿آبائِكُمُ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ an adjective; ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb); ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿فِي شَكٍّ﴾ both attached to an omitted khabar; ﴿يَلْعَبُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the verbal clause is a ḥāl, and the nominal clause is resumptive; ﴿فَارْتَقِبْ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an unstated condition), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition; ﴿تَأْتِي﴾ an imperfect verb; ﴿السَّماءُ﴾ fāʿil; ﴿بِدُخانٍ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿مُبِينٍ﴾ an adjective, and the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

daas-irab:11-18.t: ﴿يَغْشَى﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿النَّاسَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of دخان; ﴿هذا عَذابٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); ﴿أَلِيمٌ﴾ an adjective of عذاب, and the nominal clause is the object of an omitted saying (maqūl qawl maḥdhūf); ﴿رَبَّنَا﴾ the one addressed (munādā), in annexation; ﴿اكْشِفْ﴾ a verb of supplication whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿عَنَّا﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb; ﴿الْعَذابَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the clause ربنا is the object of an omitted saying; ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿مُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ its khabar, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīliyya); ﴿أَنَّى﴾ an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ) as a fronted khabar; ﴿لَهُمُ﴾ both attached to an omitted second khabar; ﴿الذِّكْرى﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is the object of an omitted saying; ﴿وَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); ﴿جاءَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿رَسُولٌ﴾ a postponed fāʿil; ﴿مُبِينٌ﴾ an adjective of رسول, and the clause is circumstantial; ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction; ﴿تَوَلَّوْا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿عَنْهُ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿وَقالُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and قالوا is conjoined to تولوا; ﴿مُعَلَّمٌ﴾ the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; ﴿مَجْنُونٌ﴾ a second khabar, and the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿كاشِفُوا﴾ its khabar; ﴿الْعَذابِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation), and the nominal clause is resumptive; ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾ an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿إِنَّكُمْ عائِدُونَ﴾ inna, its noun and its khabar, and the nominal clause is resumptive; ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb; ﴿نَبْطِشُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿الْبَطْشَةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿الْكُبْرى﴾ an adjective of البطشة, and the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿مُنْتَقِمُونَ﴾ its khabar, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is a particle of oath and of the genitive, and what is sworn by is omitted, and the lām occurs in the response to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), and قد is a particle of affirmation; ﴿فَتَنَّا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the response to the oath, with no grammatical position; ﴿قَبْلَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of time; ﴿قَوْمَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿وَجاءَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿رَسُولٌ﴾ a postponed fāʿil; ﴿كَرِيمٌ﴾ an adjective of رسول, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿أَنْ﴾ explicative (tafsīriyya); ﴿أَدُّوا﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is explicative, with no grammatical position; ﴿إِلَيَّ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿عِبادَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Divine Name, muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿إِنِّي﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿رَسُولٌ﴾ the khabar of inna; ﴿أَمِينٌ﴾ an adjective, and the nominal clause is causal.

daas-irab:19-25.t: ﴿وَأَنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and أن is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿لا تَعْلُوا﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is fāʿil (agent); ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb; ﴿إِنِّي﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿آتِيكُمْ﴾ khabar (predicate), and the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl); ﴿بِسُلْطانٍ﴾ both attached to آتيكم; ﴿مُبِينٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); ﴿وَإِنِّي﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and inna and its noun; ﴿عُذْتُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the verbal clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is circumstantial; ﴿بِرَبِّي﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿وَرَبِّكُمْ﴾ conjoined to بربي; ﴿أَنْ تَرْجُمُونِ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by أن, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), and the dropped first-person yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) formed from أن and the verb is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb عذت; ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and إن is a conditional that makes the verb jussive; ﴿لَمْ﴾ a particle making the verb jussive; ﴿تُؤْمِنُوا﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive by لم, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is initial (ibtidāʾiyya); ﴿لِي﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿فَاعْتَزِلُونِ﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the nūn is the nūn of protection, and the dropped first-person yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis; ﴿فَدَعا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); ﴿رَبَّهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is conjoined to an implied clause; ﴿أَنَّ هؤُلاءِ قَوْمٌ﴾ anna, its noun and its khabar; ﴿مُجْرِمُونَ﴾ an adjective of قوم, and the interpreted maṣdar formed from أن and what follows it is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb دعا; ﴿فَأَسْرِ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an unstated condition), and an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the weak letter, whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition; ﴿بِعِبادِي﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿لَيْلًا﴾ an adverb of time; ﴿إِنَّكُمْ مُتَّبَعُونَ﴾ inna, its noun and its khabar, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation; ﴿وَاتْرُكِ الْبَحْرَ﴾ a conjunction, and an imperative verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent; ﴿رَهْواً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿إِنَّهُمْ جُنْدٌ﴾ inna, its noun and its khabar; ﴿مُغْرَقُونَ﴾ an adjective of جند, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation; ﴿كَمْ﴾ predicative (khabariyya), in the position of the accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi; ﴿تَرَكُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿مِنْ جَنَّاتٍ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl; ﴿وَعُيُونٍ﴾ conjoined to جنات.

daas-irab:26-35.t: ﴿وَزُرُوعٍ وَمَقامٍ﴾ both conjoined to جنات; ﴿كَرِيمٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of مقام; ﴿وَنَعْمَةٍ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun; ﴿فِيها﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to فاكهين; ﴿فاكِهِينَ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of كانوا, and the verbal clause is an adjective of نعمة; ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿وَأَوْرَثْناها﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿قَوْماً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿آخَرِينَ﴾ an adjective; ﴿فَما﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, and ما is negative; ﴿بَكَتْ﴾ a past verb; ﴿عَلَيْهِمُ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿السَّماءُ﴾ fāʿil; ﴿وَالْأَرْضُ﴾ conjoined to السماء, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and ما is negative; ﴿كانُوا مُنْظَرِينَ﴾ kāna, its noun and its khabar, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, the lām occurs in the response to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), and قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); ﴿نَجَّيْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿بَنِي﴾ mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ; ﴿إِسْرائِيلَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation), and the clause نجينا is the response to the oath, with no grammatical position, and the discourse is resumptive; ﴿مِنَ الْعَذابِ﴾ both attached to نجينا; ﴿الْمُهِينِ﴾ an adjective; ﴿مِنْ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ a badal (substitute) for His words من العذاب; ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿كانَ عالِياً﴾ kāna and its khabar, and its noun is latent (mustatir), and the verbal clause is the khabar of inna; ﴿مِنَ الْمُسْرِفِينَ﴾ both attached to an omitted second khabar, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl); ﴿وَلَقَدِ اخْتَرْناهُمْ﴾ see verse no. 30 of the sura; ﴿عَلى عِلْمٍ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿عَلَى الْعالَمِينَ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿وَآتَيْناهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its first mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿مِنَ الْآياتِ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿ما﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿فِيهِ﴾ both attached to an omitted fronted khabar; ﴿بَلؤُا﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿مُبِينٌ﴾ an adjective of بلاء; ﴿إِنَّ هؤُلاءِ﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿لَيَقُولُونَ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is resumptive; ﴿إِنْ﴾ negative; ﴿هِيَ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿مَوْتَتُنَا﴾ khabar; ﴿الْأُولى﴾ an adjective, and the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, ما is negative, operating like ليس; ﴿نَحْنُ﴾ its noun; ﴿بِمُنْشَرِينَ﴾ genitive in form, accusative in position, as the khabar of ما, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:36-43.t: ﴿فَأْتُوا﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an unstated condition), and an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition; ﴿بِآبائِنا﴾ both attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb; ﴿إِنْ﴾ a conditional that makes the verb jussive; ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun; ﴿صادِقِينَ﴾ its khabar (predicate), and the verbal clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; ﴿أَهُمْ﴾ the hamza is a particle of interrogation expressing disapproval, and ﴿هُمْ﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾ khabar, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction; ﴿قَوْمُ﴾ conjoined to the pronoun; ﴿تُبَّعٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation); ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ conjoined to قوم; ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ both attached to an omitted verb forming the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative; ﴿أَهْلَكْناهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is circumstantial; ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun; ﴿مُجْرِمِينَ﴾ its khabar, and the verbal clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl); ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and ما is negative; ﴿خَلَقْنَا السَّماواتِ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ conjoined to السموات, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿وَما﴾ conjoined to السموات; ﴿بَيْنَهُما﴾ an adverb of place; ﴿لاعِبِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ; ﴿ما﴾ negative; ﴿خَلَقْناهُما﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl; ﴿وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and lākinna and its noun; ﴿لا﴾ negative; ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the verbal clause is the khabar of lākinna, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl; ﴿إِنَّ يَوْمَ﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿الْفَصْلِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿مِيقاتُهُمْ﴾ its khabar, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿أَجْمَعِينَ﴾ tawkīd (emphasis); ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ a badal (substitute) for يوم الفصل; ﴿لا﴾ negative; ﴿يُغْنِي﴾ an imperfect verb; ﴿مَوْلًى﴾ its fāʿil; ﴿عَنْ مَوْلًى﴾ both attached to the verb, and the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and لا is negative; ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception; ﴿مَنْ﴾ excepted by إلا; ﴿رَحِمَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila of من; ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿هُوَ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); ﴿الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ﴾ two khabars, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation; ﴿إِنَّ شَجَرَةَ﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿الزَّقُّومِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi.

daas-irab:44-53.t: ﴿طَعامُ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of inna; ﴿الْأَثِيمِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation); ﴿كَالْمُهْلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted second khabar; ﴿يَغْلِي﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿فِي الْبُطُونِ﴾ both attached to the verb, and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿كَغَلْيِ﴾ both attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿الْحَمِيمِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿خُذُوهُ﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the hāʾ is its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the object of an omitted saying (maqūl qawl maḥdhūf); ﴿فَاعْتِلُوهُ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperative verb conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿إِلى سَواءِ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿الْجَحِيمِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction; ﴿صُبُّوا﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil; ﴿فَوْقَ﴾ an adverb of place; ﴿رَأْسِهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿مِنْ عَذابِ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿الْحَمِيمِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿ذُقْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the object of an omitted saying; ﴿إِنَّكَ﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿أَنْتَ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); ﴿الْعَزِيزُ الْكَرِيمُ﴾ two khabars, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīliyya); ﴿إِنَّ هذا﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿ما﴾ its khabar; ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما; ﴿بِهِ﴾ both attached to تمترون; ﴿تَمْتَرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of كنتم, and the clause إن هذا is the object of an implied saying; ﴿إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿فِي مَقامٍ﴾ both attached to the omitted khabar of inna; ﴿أَمِينٍ﴾ an adjective; ﴿فِي جَنَّاتٍ﴾ a badal (substitute) for في مقام; ﴿وَعُيُونٍ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it «[Translator's note: the source text is garbled at this point (the brackets around في جنات and وعيون are corrupted); the reading given here follows the evident intent.]»; ﴿يَلْبَسُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is a second khabar of inna; ﴿مِنْ سُندُسٍ﴾ both attached to an omitted adjective of the omitted object; ﴿وَإِسْتَبْرَقٍ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿مُتَقابِلِينَ﴾ ḥāl.

daas-irab:54-59.t: ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "الأمر كذلك" (the matter is thus); ﴿وَزَوَّجْناهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is conjoined to the clause يلبسون; ﴿بِحُورٍ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿عِينٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); ﴿يَدْعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; ﴿فِيها﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿بِكُلِّ﴾ both attached to the verb as well; ﴿فاكِهَةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation); ﴿آمِنِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), and the clause is circumstantial; ﴿لا يَذُوقُونَ﴾ لا is negative, and an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is circumstantial; ﴿فِيهَا﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿الْمَوْتَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception; ﴿الْمَوْتَةَ﴾ excepted; ﴿الْأُولى﴾ an adjective of الموتة; ﴿وَوَقاهُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir); ﴿عَذابَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿الْجَحِيمِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause is circumstantial; ﴿فَضْلًا﴾ an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) «[Translator's note: so in the source; presumably meaning a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb.]»; ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ both attached to فضلا; ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ; ﴿هُوَ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); ﴿الْفَوْزُ﴾ the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; ﴿الْعَظِيمُ﴾ an adjective, and the nominal clause ذلك is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿فَإِنَّما﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, and the restraining (kāffa) and the restrained (makfūfa); ﴿يَسَّرْناهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is resumptive; ﴿بِلِسانِكَ﴾ both attached to the verb; ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ﴾ laʿalla and its noun; ﴿يَتَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar of laʿalla, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl); ﴿فَارْتَقِبْ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an unstated condition), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ inna and its noun; ﴿مُرْتَقِبُونَ﴾ its khabar, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position, and the verbal clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, with no grammatical position.

farraa:4-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ﴾.
﴿أَمْراً﴾ is accusative by His saying يفرق, in the sense: every affair is distinguished, a distinguishing (farqan) and a command (amran); and likewise.
His saying: ﴿رَحْمَةً مِّن رَّبِّكَ﴾: that is distinguished as a mercy from your Lord. And it is allowed to put الرحمة in the accusative by مرسلين falling upon it, making the mercy the Prophet himself, Allah bless him.

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying: ﴿رَبِّ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
Al-Aʿmash and his companions put it in the genitive, and the people of Medina put it in the nominative. Al-Ḥasan also put it in the genitive, so that it follows ربك: "your Lord, the Lord of the heavens".
Whoever puts it in the nominative makes it follow His saying: ﴿إنهُ هُوَ السَّميعُ العَلِيمُ﴾; and another also put it in the nominative by resumption (istiʾnāf), as He said: "وما بينهُما الرحمنُ".

farraa:10-11.t:
His saying: ﴿تَأْتِي ٱلسَّمَآءُ بِدُخَانٍ مُّبِينٍ يَغْشَى ٱلنَّاسَ هَـٰذَا عَذَابٌ﴾.
The Prophet, Allah bless him, had prayed against them, saying: "O Allah, make Your tread heavy upon Muḍar; O Allah, [send on them years] like the years of Joseph." So hunger struck them until they ate bones and carrion, and they would see between themselves and the sky [something like] smoke.
His saying: ﴿يَغْشَى ٱلنَّاسَ هَـٰذَا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾.
By it is meant: that is a punishment. And it is said that the people were saying: "This smoke is a punishment."

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّا كَاشِفُو ٱلْعَذَابِ قَلِيلاً إِنَّكُمْ عَآئِدُونَ﴾.
It is said: returning to your shirk; and it is said: returning to the punishment of the Hereafter.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ﴾.
He means: the Day of Badr, and it is the greatest assault.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿رَسُولٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾.
I.e. honoured with his Lord; and it may be "noble among his people", because he said: no prophet was sent except that he was of the noblest of his people.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿أَنْ أَدُّوۤاْ إِلَيَّ عِبَادَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
He says: hand them over to me, send them with me; and that is His saying: ﴿أَرْسِلْ مَعِىَ بَنىِ إِسْرَائيلَ﴾.
And it is said: "Render to me [your obedience], O servants of Allah"; in the first interpretation العباد is accusative by أدوا.

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿أَن تَرْجُمُونِ﴾.
Al-rajm (stoning) here is killing.

farraa:21-21.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِن لَّمْ تُؤْمِنُواْ لِي فَٱعْتَزِلُونِ﴾.
He says: then leave me, neither against me nor for me.

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿فَدَعَا رَبَّهُ أَنَّ هَـٰؤُلاَءِ قَوْمٌ﴾.
You give (أنَّ) fatḥa; and had you implied a verb of saying and given it kasra, it would have been correct.

farraa:24-24.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱتْرُكِ ٱلْبَحْرَ رَهْواً﴾.
He says: still. He said: and Abū Tharwān recited to me:
كأنما أهلُ حجر ينظرون مَتى * يَرَونَنى خارجاً طير تَنَادِيد طيرٌ رأَتْ بازياً نَضْخُ الدماءِ به * أو أمةٌ خرجَتْ رهواً إلى عيد
(It is as if the people of Ḥajr, watching for when they will see me coming out, are scattering birds: birds that have seen a falcon spattered with blood, or a slave-girl who went out leisurely (rahwan) to a festival.)

farraa:26-29.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَقَامٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾.
It is said: fine dwellings; and it is said: the pulpits.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Abū Shuʿayb narrated to me, from Manṣūr ibn al-Muʿtamir, from al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying: ﴿فَمَا بَكَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ وَٱلأَرْضُ﴾: he said: for the believer, his place of prayer on earth weeps over him, and the place in heaven where his deeds ascend weeps over him.
Al-Farrāʾ said: and so Ḥibbān reported it, from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās.

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿مِنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلْمُهِينِ﴾; and in the text (ḥarf) of ʿAbd Allāh: "مِنْ عَذَابِ المُهِين".
This is among what is annexed to itself because the two nouns differ, like His saying: ﴿ولَدَارُ الآخِرَةِ خيرٌ﴾, and like His saying: ﴿وذَلِكَ دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ﴾, which in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh is: "وذلك الدينُ القَيِّمَةُ".

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُم مِّنَ ٱلآيَاتِ مَا فِيهِ بَلاَءٌ مُّبِينٌ﴾.
He means: clear favours, among them that He saved them from the people of Pharaoh, shaded them with clouds, and sent down to them manna and quails. It is as you say to a man: "My favour (balāʾ) towards you is surely good." And it has been said concerning them that al-balāʾ is punishment; and all is correct.

farraa:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأْتُواْ بِآبَآئِنَا إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾.
They address the Prophet, Allah bless him, alone; and it is like His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها النَّبىُّ إذا طلَّقتُمُ النِّساءَ﴾. In much of the speech of the Arabs, the Arabs put the action of one in the plural; of that is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ أرْجِعونِ﴾.

farraa:39-39.t:
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ بِٱلْحَقِّ﴾.
He means: for the truth.

farraa:40-40.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ يَوْمَ ٱلْفَصْلِ مِيقَاتُهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾.
He means: the first and the last. Had ﴿مِيقَاتُهم﴾ been put in the accusative, it would have been correct, making "the day" an adverb (ṣifa). He said: one of them recited to me:
لو كنت أعلم أنّ آخر عهدكم * يوم الرحيل فعلت ما لم أفعل
(Had I known that my last meeting with you was on the day of departure, I would have done what I did not do.)
So he put يوم الرحيل in the accusative, as an adverb (ṣifa).
«[Translator's note: ṣifa here is al-Farrāʾ's Kufan term for the adverbial (ẓarf), not "adjective".]»

farraa:42-42.t:
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ مَن رَّحِمَ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
For the believers intercede for one another. If you wish, make مَن in the position of the nominative, as though you said: "No one stands except so-and-so"; and if you wish, you make it accusative by exception (istithnāʾ), cut off from the beginning of the speech, meaning: "O Allah, except whom You have had mercy upon."

farraa:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿طَعَامُ ٱلأَثِيمِ﴾.
He means: the wicked.

farraa:45-45.t:
His saying: ﴿كَٱلْمُهْلِ تَغْلِي﴾.
Many of the companions of ʿAbd Allāh read it: "تغلى", and it has been reported from ʿAbd Allāh, and the people of Medina read it likewise; and al-Ḥasan read it "يغلى", making it refer to the food or to the muhl (molten brass). Whoever makes it feminine refers to the feminine of the tree.
Like it is His saying: ﴿أَمَنَةً نُعاساً﴾: تغشى and يغشى; the masculine is for the drowsiness (nuʿās), and the feminine for the security (amana). And like it: ﴿أَلَمْ يَكُ نُطْفَةً مِنْ مَّنِىٍّ تُمْنَى﴾: the feminine is for the nuṭfa (drop), and the masculine from the manī (semen).

farraa:47-47.t:
His saying: ﴿فَٱعْتِلُوهُ﴾.
ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read it with kasra, and the people of Medina read it: "فاعتلُوه", with ḍamma on the tāʾ.

farraa:49-49.t:
His saying: ﴿ذُقْ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْكَرِيمُ﴾.
The readers read it with kasra on the alif. Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: a shaykh narrated to me, from Ḥujr, from Abū Qatāda al-Anṣārī, from his father, who said: I heard al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib say on the pulpit: "ذُقْ أَنك", with fatḥa on the alif. The meaning with fatḥa is: taste, because of this saying which you said in the world. Whoever uses kasra relates his saying. That is because Abū Jahl met the Prophet, Allah bless him; he said: the Prophet, Allah bless him, took hold of him and shook him, then said [to him]: "Woe to you, O Abū Jahl, woe!" And Allah sent it down as the Prophet, Allah bless him, said it. Abū Jahl answered him and said: "[By] Allah, neither you nor your Lord has power over me; I am the most honoured of the people of the valley among his people, and the mightiest of them." So it was revealed as he had said it. He said: so its meaning, as we see it, and Allah knows best, is that it is a rebuke, i.e. [173/b] taste, for you are honoured as you claimed, while you are not so.

farraa:51-51.t:
His saying: ﴿فِي مَقَامٍ أَمِينٍ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim read it: ﴿مَقامٍ﴾, and the people of Medina read it (فى مُقام), with ḍamma on the mīm.
Al-maqām with fatḥa on the mīm is better in Arabic, because it is the place; and al-muqām is the staying; and all is correct.

farraa:54-54.t:
His saying: ﴿وَزَوَّجْنَاهُم بِحُورٍ عِينٍ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "وَأَمْدَدْناهُمْ بِعِيسٍ عِين"; al-ʿaysāʾ is the white one, and al-ḥawrāʾ likewise.

farraa:56-57.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا ٱلْمَوْتَ إِلاَّ ٱلْمَوْتَةَ ٱلأُولَىٰ﴾.
Someone may say: how did He except a death in the world that has passed from the death of the Hereafter? This is like His saying: ﴿ولا تَنْكِحُوا ما نَكَحَ آباؤُكم من النِّساءِ إِلاَّ ما قَدْ سَلَفَ﴾: إلا in this place is in the position of سوى (other than), as though He said: do not marry, do not do other than what your fathers did. Likewise His saying: ﴿لا يذُوقون فيها الموتَ﴾: other than the first death. And like it: ﴿خالدِينَ فيها ما دَامتِ السّماوَاتُ والأرضُ إِلا مَا شَاءَ ربُّك﴾, i.e. besides what your Lord has willed for them of addition of immortality beyond the measure of the world. And you say in speech: "You have a thousand with me, except (إلا) what you have through so-and-so", and its meaning is: besides what you have with me through so-and-so. So إلا may be a subtraction from what precedes it or an addition to it. What we have mentioned to you of these verses is an addition to what precedes إلا; and subtraction from what precedes إلا is your saying: "These are a thousand except a hundred", the meaning being: they are a thousand less a hundred.
His saying: ﴿وَوَقَاهُمْ عَذَابَ ٱلْجَحِيمِ فضلاً﴾.
I.e. He did it as a favour from Him; and it is among what, had it come in the nominative, would have been correct, i.e.: that is a favour from your Lord.

zajjaj:10-10.t:
And His saying: ﴿فارْتَقِبْ يَوْمَ تَأْتِي السَّماءُ بِدُخانٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ ﴿يَغْشى النّاسَ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 11]: "فارْتَقِبْ" means: so wait. In most of the exegesis, the smoke has already passed: that was when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invoked against Muḍar, saying: «"O Allah, make Your tread heavy upon Muḍar, and make it years upon them like the years of Joseph,"» that is, make their years of drought like the years of Joseph. The Arabs also call drought "اَلسَّنَةَ" (the year), so the meaning would be: "Make it droughts upon them." So the rain was withheld, the land became barren, and between the sky and the earth there was something like smoke.
And His saying: ﴿هَذا عَذابٌ ألِيمٌ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 11]: the meaning is: the people upon whom the drought descends say: "This is a painful punishment"; and likewise His saying: ﴿رَبَّنا اكْشِفْ عَنّا العَذابَ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 12].

zajjaj:15-15.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنّا كاشِفُو العَذابِ قَلِيلا إنَّكم عائِدُونَ﴾: "أنَّكم عائِدُونَ" is also permissible; whoever reads "أنَّكم عائِدُونَ", that is the [proper] way. The meaning is that He informs them that they will not take admonition, and that when the hateful thing is removed from them they will return to their transgression.
«[Translator's note: as printed, the source calls the fatḥa reading "أنَّكم" "the proper way" (al-wajh), though the canonical text has "إنَّكم" with kasra; the source may intend the kasra reading here.]»

zajjaj:16-16.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ البَطْشَةَ الكُبْرى إنّا مُنْتَقِمُونَ﴾: "يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ" and "نَبْطُشُ" ﴿إنّا مُنْتَقِمُونَ﴾: this is like "عَكَفَ، يَعْكُفُ، ويَعْكِفُ" and "عَرَشَ، يَعْرِشُ، ويَعْرُشُ", and this is frequent in the language. It has been said that the greatest seizure is the day of Badr. "يَوْمَ" cannot be accusative by His saying "مُنْتَقِمُونَ", because what comes after "إنّا" cannot govern what precedes it; rather, it is accusative by [an implied] "واذْكُرْ يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ البَطْشَةَ الكُبْرى" (and remember the day We seize with the greatest seizure).

zajjaj:17-17.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ فَتَنّا قَبْلَهم قَوْمَ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾, up to His saying: ﴿أنْ أدُّوا إلَيَّ عِبادَ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 18]. The meaning of "أنْ أدُّوا إلَيَّ عِبادَ اللَّهِ" is: hand over to me the servants of Allah, meaning the Children of Israel, as He said: ﴿فَأرْسِلْ مَعَنا بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ ولا تُعَذِّبْهُمْ﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 47], that is, release them from your torment. It is also permissible that "عِبادَ اللَّهِ" be accusative as a vocative (nidāʾ), so the meaning would be: "Render to me what Allah has commanded you, O servants of Allah."

zajjaj:19-19.t: ﴿وَأنْ لا تَعْلُوا عَلى اللَّهِ إنِّي آتِيكم بِسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ﴾: that is, with a clear, evident proof, showing that I am a prophet.

zajjaj:2-2.t:
Sūrat al-Dukhān
Meccan
﷽
It has come in the exegesis: Whoever recites Sūrat "al-Dukhān" on the eve of Friday, affirming and believing, Allah will forgive him. We have explained the meaning of "حـم" earlier.
And His saying: ﴿والكِتابِ المُبِينِ﴾ is an oath.

zajjaj:20-20.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَإنِّي عُذْتُ بِرَبِّي ورَبِّكم أنْ تَرْجُمُونِ﴾: that is, lest you kill me.
And His saying: ﴿وَإنْ لَمْ تُؤْمِنُوا لِي فاعْتَزِلُونِ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 21]: that is, if you do not believe me, then be neither against me nor with me.

zajjaj:22-22.t: ﴿فَدَعا رَبَّهُ أنَّ هَؤُلاءِ قَوْمٌ مُجْرِمُونَ﴾: Whoever reads "إنَّ" with kasra, the meaning is: "He said: These are…", and "إنَّ" after [a verb of] saying is with kasra. The fatḥa is permissible with the meaning "فَدَعا رَبَّهُ بِأنَّ هَؤُلاءِ" (so he called upon his Lord [saying] that these…).

zajjaj:24-24.t: And His saying: ﴿واتْرُكِ البَحْرَ رَهْوًا﴾: It has come in the exegesis: "dry," as He said: ﴿فاضْرِبْ لَهم طَرِيقًا في البَحْرِ يَبَسًا﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 77]. The lexicographers said: "رَهْوًا" means still.

zajjaj:25-25.t: And His saying: ﴿كَمْ تَرَكُوا مِن جَنّاتٍ وعُيُونٍ﴾ ﴿وَزُرُوعٍ ومَقامٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 26]: It has come in the exegesis that the noble place (al-maqām al-karīm) here means the pulpits; and it has come concerning "مَقامٍ كَرِيمٍ": that is, in fine dwellings.

zajjaj:28-28.t: His saying: ﴿كَذَلِكَ وأوْرَثْناها قَوْمًا آخَرِينَ﴾: the meaning is "the matter is thus"; the position of "كَذَلِكَ" is nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an implied (muḍmar) mubtadaʾ (subject).

zajjaj:29-29.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَما بَكَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّماءُ والأرْضُ﴾: because they died as disbelievers. When the believers die, the heaven and the earth weep for them: of the earth, the believer's place of prayer weeps for him, that is, the place where he prayed; and of the heaven, the place where his deeds ascend and where his provision descends. It has come in the exegesis that the earth weeps for the believer for forty mornings.
And His saying: ﴿وَما كانُوا مُنْظَرِينَ﴾: that is, they were not granted a delay of the punishment. ﴿وَلَقَدِ اخْتَرْناهم عَلى عِلْمٍ عَلى العالَمِينَ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 32]: that is, over the peoples of their age.

zajjaj:3-3.t: And His saying: ﴿إنّا أنْـزَلْناهُ في لَيْلَةٍ مُبارَكَةٍ﴾: It has come in the exegesis that it is the Night of Decree (laylat al-qadr). Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إنّا أنْـزَلْناهُ في لَيْلَةِ القَدْرِ﴾ [al-Qadr: 1]. The exegetes said: "في لَيْلَةٍ مُبارَكَةٍ" is the Night of Decree; it was sent down all at once to the lowest heaven on the Night of Decree, then sent down to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ piece by piece.

zajjaj:34-34.t: And His saying: ﴿إنَّ هَؤُلاءِ لَيَقُولُونَ﴾ ﴿إنْ هي إلا مَوْتَتُنا الأُولى وما نَحْنُ بِمُنْشَرِينَ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 35]: this was said by the disbelievers of Quraysh. The meaning of "إنْ هي" is "it is not (mā hiya)," and the meaning of "بِمُنْشَرِينَ" is "to be resurrected." One says "أنْشَرَ اللَّهُ المَوْتى" (Allah raised the dead) and "نُشِرُوا هم" (they were raised).

zajjaj:37-37.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أهم خَيْرٌ أمْ قَوْمُ تُبَّعٍ﴾: It has come in the exegesis that Tubbaʿ was a believer and that his people were disbelievers. And it has come that he looked at an inscription on two graves in the region of Ḥimyar: on the grave of one of them, "This is the grave of Raḍwā," and on the other, "This is the grave of Ḥubbā," the two daughters of Tubbaʿ, who associated nothing with Allah.
«[Translator's note: the subject of "نَظَرَ" (he looked) is not named in the source; it may be an unnamed narrator rather than Tubbaʿ.]»

zajjaj:39-39.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ما خَلَقْناهُما إلا بِالحَقِّ﴾: by it are meant the heavens and the earth; that is, only for the establishment of the truth.

zajjaj:4-4.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فِيها يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ﴾: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, on the Night of Decree, apportions every matter in which there is wisdom, of the provisions of the servants, their terms of life, and all their affairs, which are appointed until the Night of Decree that falls in the following year.

zajjaj:40-40.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّ يَوْمَ الفَصْلِ مِيقاتُهم أجْمَعِينَ﴾: "مِيقاتَهم", with the tāʾ in the accusative, is also permissible, but I do not know that it has been read so, so do not ever read it so. Whoever reads "مِيقاتُهم" in the nominative makes "يَوْمَ الفَصْلِ" the noun (ism) of "إنَّ" and makes "مِيقاتُهم" the khabar (predicate). Whoever makes "مِيقاتَهم" accusative makes it the noun of "إنَّ" and makes "يَوْمَ الفَصْلِ" accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), the meaning being: "Their appointed time is on the Day of Decision."

zajjaj:41-41.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَوْمَ لا يُغْنِي مَوْلًى عَنْ مَوْلًى شَيْئًا﴾: no ally will avail his ally anything, nor a father his child, nor a child his father.

zajjaj:43-43.t: And His saying: ﴿إنَّ شَجَرَتَ الزَّقُّومِ﴾ ﴿طَعامُ الأثِيمِ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 44]: by it [the sinner] is meant here Abū Jahl ibn Hishām. And "اَلْمُهْلُ" is the dregs of oil; and it is also said: "اَلْمُهْلُ" is whatever is molten of silver, copper and the like.

zajjaj:47-47.t: And His saying: ﴿خُذُوهُ فاعْتِلُوهُ﴾: It is also read "فاعْتُلُوهُ" — with ḍamma on the tāʾ, and with kasra. The meaning is: "O angels, seize him and drag him." "اَلْعَتْلُ" is that one is seized and taken off with harshness and violence. ﴿إلى سَواءِ الجَحِيمِ﴾: to the middle of Hellfire.

zajjaj:49-49.t: And His saying: ﴿ذُقْ إنَّكَ أنْتَ العَزِيزُ الكَرِيمُ﴾: All the people [readers] have the kasra in "إنَّكَ" except al-Kisāʾī alone, who read "ذُقْ أنَّكَ أنْتَ", that is: because you said, "You are indeed the mighty, the noble." That is because he [Abū Jahl] used to say: "I am the mightiest and best-defended of the people of this valley." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: "Taste this punishment; you are the one who said: I am the mighty, the noble."

zajjaj:5-5.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أمْرًا مِن عِنْدِنا﴾.
And His saying: ﴿رَحْمَةً مِن رَبِّكَ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 6]: both are accusative. Al-Akhfash said: as ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "We sent it down, commanding a command and being merciful with mercy." It is also possible that it is accusative by "يُفْرَقُ", in the position of "يَفْرُقُ فَرْقًا" (a mafʿūl muṭlaq, absolute object), because "أمْرًا" has the meaning of "فَرْقًا", since the meaning is "a command is enjoined in it." And it is possible that "رَحْمَةً مِن رَبِّكَ" is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), that is: "We sent it down as a mercy," that is, "for the sake of mercy."

zajjaj:51-51.t: And His saying: ﴿إنَّ المُتَّقِينَ في مَقامٍ أمِينٍ﴾: that is, in it they are safe from changes of fortune.

zajjaj:53-53.t: And His saying: ﴿يَلْبَسُونَ مِن سُنْدُسٍ وإسْتَبْرَقٍ مُتَقابِلِينَ﴾: It has been said: "اَلْإسْتَبْرَقُ" is thick brocade, and "اَلسُّنْدُسُ" is silk. It was called "إسْتَبْرَقٌ" — and Allah knows best — only because of the intensity of its sheen (barīq).

zajjaj:56-56.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لا يَذُوقُونَ فِيها المَوْتَ إلا المَوْتَةَ الأُولى﴾: the meaning is: they will not taste death in it at all, apart from the first death which they tasted in this world. The two [verses] are as He said: ﴿وَلا تَنْكِحُوا ما نَكَحَ آباؤُكم مِنَ النِّساءِ إلا ما قَدْ سَلَفَ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 22].

zajjaj:57-57.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَضْلا مِن رَبِّكَ﴾: "فَضْلٌ مِن رَبِّكَ" is also permissible, but it must not be read so, because it contradicts the codex. The accusative is on the meaning of His saying ﴿يَدْعُونَ فِيها بِكُلِّ فاكِهَةٍ آمِنِينَ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 55], and on the meaning of ﴿إنَّ المُتَّقِينَ في مَقامٍ أمِينٍ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 51], and that is by a bounty from Allah; so the meaning is: "Allah did that for them as a bounty from Him and a favour from Him."

zajjaj:59-59.t: And His saying: ﴿فارْتَقِبْ إنَّهم مُرْتَقِبُونَ﴾: its meaning is: "So wait; they too are waiting."

zajjaj:7-7.t: And His saying: ﴿رَبِّ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ وما بَيْنَهُما﴾: with the genitive and the nominative. The nominative is as a description (ṣifa), and the genitive is on [the basis of] His saying "مِن رَبِّكَ رَبِّ السَّماواتِ" (from your Lord, the Lord of the heavens). Whoever reads the nominative, it is on [the basis of] His saying: "إنَّهُ هو السَّمِيعُ العَلِيمُ رَبُّ السَّماواتِ"; or, if you wish, as resumptive (istiʾnāf), with the meaning: "He is the Lord of the heavens."

zajjaj:8-8.t: And His saying: ﴿لا إلَهَ إلا هو يُحْيِي ويُمِيتُ رَبُّكم ورَبُّ آبائِكُمُ الأوَّلِينَ﴾: It is also read "رَبِّكم ورَبِّ آبائِكُمُ الأوَّلِينَ". The genitive is with the meaning "رَحْمَةً مِن رَبِّكَ رَبِّكم ورَبِّ آبائِكُمُ الأوَّلِينَ" (a mercy from your Lord, your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers).
